# v0.9.7 evidence: blame's provenance map kept through outside edits, and checked

Every figure cites the run that printed it (`[run JOB/RUN:field]`: the run records in
`docs/evidence/runs/`, checked by `tools/evidence/check.py`). Measured numbers only.

**The finding first.** Blame does not rebuild its map after every change, and hasn't since
v0.9.0: the session's own changes (edits, `write --base`, undo, redo, revert, restore) keep it
up to date as they apply (`Prov::apply`, O(the change)). Until v0.9.5, three paths dropped
it, so the next blame (or edit) rebuilt it on a throwaway replica, O(the doc's history):
**an outside edit**, a purge and a recovery (and a load: the cold path). v0.9.5 keeps it
through outside edits; a purge, a recovery and a load stay cold. The soak makes no outside
edits, so this change can't move it, and it doesn't (below).

## Blame's cost at three history sizes

`crates/base/tests/blame_cost.rs`, `blame_cost_at_sizes`. Before: node job `348445a2` (v0.9.3
plus only this test: scratch commit `10eb847`, never merged). After: node job `72ccab9a`
(`1807c7b`, v0.9.3 plus this change). Neither the rebase onto v0.9.4 nor the fix the
differential test found (`338b792`: an extra engine walk only when an outside edit leaves a
root's text as it was) changes what these scenarios run.

- **Node and settings:** a build node, both jobs `--exclusive --cpus 4 --mem 8G`, one after the
  other, release, one test thread.
- **The history:** built through a session (public API only): a 300-line file and four agents
  taking turns, a line in at the top, the last line out. The text stays about 300 lines; the
  engine's state keeps every deleted line. The build isn't timed.
- **What was timed:** each `blame` call alone (`Instant`), after one warm-up blame. Per size:
  10 blames after an outside edit (the write-back and the ingest not timed); 30 of every line
  and 30 of `-L 100,109`, each after an agent's edit; 5 cold (each after the store is
  reopened). p50 in µs:

| History (changes) | Blame | Before (v0.9.3) | After (v0.9.5) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,200 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_1200_outside:changes] | after an outside edit | 1,285 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_1200_outside:p50_us] | **845 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_1200_outside:p50_us]** |
| 1,200 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_1200_steady:changes] | after an edit, every line | 819 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_1200_steady:p50_us] | **819 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_1200_steady:p50_us]** |
| 1,200 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_1200_range:changes] | after an edit, lines 100 to 109 | 51 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_1200_range:p50_us] | **50 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_1200_range:p50_us]** |
| 1,200 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_1200_cold:changes] | first after a reopen (cold) | 1,363 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_1200_cold:p50_us] | **1,404 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_1200_cold:p50_us]** |
| 40,000 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_40000_outside:changes] | after an outside edit | 9,408 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_40000_outside:p50_us] | **1,107 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_40000_outside:p50_us]** |
| 40,000 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_40000_steady:changes] | after an edit, every line | 1,024 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_40000_steady:p50_us] | **1,031 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_40000_steady:p50_us]** |
| 40,000 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_40000_range:changes] | after an edit, lines 100 to 109 | 58 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_40000_range:p50_us] | **57 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_40000_range:p50_us]** |
| 40,000 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_40000_cold:changes] | first after a reopen (cold) | 9,637 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_40000_cold:p50_us] | **10,133 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_40000_cold:p50_us]** |
| 300,000 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_300000_outside:changes] | after an outside edit | 82,950 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_300000_outside:p50_us] | **1,323 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_300000_outside:p50_us]** |
| 300,000 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_300000_steady:changes] | after an edit, every line | 1,117 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_300000_steady:p50_us] | **1,120 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_300000_steady:p50_us]** |
| 300,000 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_300000_range:changes] | after an edit, lines 100 to 109 | 63 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_300000_range:p50_us] | **62 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_300000_range:p50_us]** |
| 300,000 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_300000_cold:changes] | first after a reopen (cold) | 92,006 [run 348445a2/blame_cost_before_300000_cold:p50_us] | **97,061 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_300000_cold:p50_us]** |

- **After an outside edit,** blame no longer grows with the history. Before, it was a rebuild,
  O(history); now it is the steady cost plus the change. At 300k changes it is 63× faster
  [derived].
- **Steady and range** are the same before and after (the map was already kept). They grow
  with the lines asked for, not with the history.
- **Cold** is the same code before and after; the after job was 3–6% slower there [derived],
  which is the noise between two runs of one binary layout against another.

## The runtime check's cost (`Config::blame_check_every`, default 1 in 100)

Same job (`72ccab9a`, `blame_check_cost`): a session with the check at 1 in 1, each size built
the same way, 10 blames of every line, each after an edit. A sampled blame rebuilds the map (a
throwaway replica) and compares it with the kept one. p50 in µs:

| History | Sampled blame | Unsampled (steady, above) | Extra per blame at 1 in 100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.2k | 1,226 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_1200_check:p50_us] | 819 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_1200_steady:p50_us] | 4 µs [derived] |
| 40k | 9,847 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_40000_check:p50_us] | 1,031 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_40000_steady:p50_us] | 88 µs [derived] |
| 300k | 105,657 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_300000_check:p50_us] | 1,120 [run 72ccab9a/blame_cost_after_300000_steady:p50_us] | 1,045 µs [derived] |

A sampled blame costs a cold rebuild. At the default rate, that adds about 1 ms per blame at
300k changes on average, against about 1.1 ms for the blame itself.

## The sampled check off the session's lock (v0.9.7)

`blame_check_cost` with a lock probe: a second thread calls `status` (it takes the session's
lock and does almost nothing) in a loop while each sampled blame runs; the longest wait of a
call that started during the blame is the lock hold the blame imposed on everyone else. Before:
node job `f5e4bdd5` (`813e4f9`, the check under the lock); after: `e22a8591` (`3f53bfd`, the
rebuild off the lock). The same node, both `--exclusive --cpus 4 --mem 8G`, one after the other,
release; the check at 1 in 1, 10 sampled blames per size. p50 in µs:

| History | Lock wait, before | **Lock wait, after** | The sampled blame's own time, before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.2k | 1,187 [run f5e4bdd5/blame_cost_lock_before_1200_check_lock_wait:p50_us] | **846 [run e22a8591/blame_cost_lock_after_1200_check_lock_wait:p50_us]** | 1,224 [run f5e4bdd5/blame_cost_lock_before_1200_check:p50_us] | 1,455 [run e22a8591/blame_cost_lock_after_1200_check:p50_us] |
| 40k | 9,626 [run f5e4bdd5/blame_cost_lock_before_40000_check_lock_wait:p50_us] | **2,223 [run e22a8591/blame_cost_lock_after_40000_check_lock_wait:p50_us]** | 9,637 [run f5e4bdd5/blame_cost_lock_before_40000_check:p50_us] | 16,781 [run e22a8591/blame_cost_lock_after_40000_check:p50_us] |
| 300k | 104,358 [run f5e4bdd5/blame_cost_lock_before_300000_check_lock_wait:p50_us] | **21,440 [run e22a8591/blame_cost_lock_after_300000_check_lock_wait:p50_us]** | 104,409 [run f5e4bdd5/blame_cost_lock_before_300000_check:p50_us] | 154,794 [run e22a8591/blame_cost_lock_after_300000_check:p50_us] |

- **The stall others see** drops 5× at 300k changes [derived]. What remains under the lock is
  the blame itself and **encoding the doc's state** for the copy the rebuild walks, O(the
  engine state). Removing that needs a snapshot from the engine (a read-only or copy-on-write
  view of the doc): a question for the engine's owners.
- **The sampled caller waits longer** (about 1.5× at 300k [derived]): the rebuild loads the
  copy, then the engine's blame walk makes its own throwaway replica of it. An engine call
  that walks a doc it may consume would halve it.
- The differential test passed again at `3f53bfd` (job `2b4a1150`): 10,000 [run 2b4a1150/blame_diff:cases]
  histories, 238,722 [run 2b4a1150/blame_diff:steps] steps, **0 [run 2b4a1150/blame_diff:reported]**
  mismatches; the planted faults were caught as before. `blame_check_off_the_lock` covers an
  edit and a purge landing between the snapshot and the verdict.

## The differential test and the planted faults

`crates/base/tests/blame_incremental.rs`, node job `faf02d89` at `338b792`: a build node, `--cpus 4
--mem 8G`, **debug** build (the kit's debug assertions on, I1 among them), 4 threads.

**The differential test** (`blame_kept_map_equals_the_rebuild`, seed 0): random docs and
histories, 24 steps each. The steps mix multi-hunk edits by a person, an agent and an assistant
acting for the person; approvals; `write --base`; undo and redo (one or two steps, partial or
all); revert; restore; purge (by change, by text, with and without `and_remove`); outside edits,
with and without a write-back first; flushes; ticks; compaction; and restarts. **After every
step:**
- the kept map equals a rebuild from the engine and the store: every root's runs (IDs and
  roots) and the live restorations by root;
- `blame` of every line, and of a random `-L` range, equals blame from the rebuild in every
  field;
- no mismatch was reported.

| | |
|---|---|
| Histories | 10,000 [run faf02d89/blame_diff:cases] |
| Steps | 238,716 [run faf02d89/blame_diff:steps] |
| Checks on a kept map (the incremental path) | 221,535 [run faf02d89/blame_diff:kept_checks] |
| Checks right after a restart or a purge (cold) | 18,465 [run faf02d89/blame_diff:cold_checks] |
| Outside edits | 26,470 [run faf02d89/blame_diff:outside_edits] |
| Lines compared | 929,008 [run faf02d89/blame_diff:lines_compared] |
| `-L` ranges compared | 232,806 [run faf02d89/blame_diff:ranges_compared] |
| Lines with `restored_by` / `erased` / an approval | 51,694 [run faf02d89/blame_diff:restored_lines] / 19,903 [run faf02d89/blame_diff:erased_lines] / 125,924 [run faf02d89/blame_diff:approval_lines] |
| Mismatches | **0 [run faf02d89/blame_diff:reported]** |

- **It found one bug before this run,** in this change, never released. Job `a0c863df` (at
  `d8b2d3a`) stopped at history 5518. An outside edit, merged into a doc with an unsynced
  edit, deleted `xy` and typed it again: the root's text was unchanged on new elements, and
  the map update skipped roots whose text hadn't changed. Fixed in `338b792`, with seed 5518
  kept as a regression test (`blame_regression_seeds`).
- `kit:unknown` (text from a client the store has no owner for) can't be reached through the
  public API: it needs a damaged log. The unit test `live_doc_untouched_and_unknown_clients`
  makes some with a raw update. It then checks the kept map and blame against the rebuild
  through edits and an undo over it, `kit:unknown` lines included.

**Planted faults** (`ProvMutant`, the `differential` feature; one change per undo or redo
call so the check runs between changes), 256 histories of 40 steps each:

| Fault | Differential: histories where it was found | Runtime check at 1 in 1: mismatches reported | Lines served, every one equal to the rebuild's |
|---|---|---|---|
| A missed deletion (the map keeps deleted elements) | 256 [run faf02d89/blame_mutant_diff_miss_deletion:found] of 256 | 4,670 [run faf02d89/blame_mutant_runtime_miss_deletion:reported] | 41,232 [run faf02d89/blame_mutant_runtime_miss_deletion:lines_served] |
| A missed deletion in the index of live restorations | 195 [run faf02d89/blame_mutant_diff_miss_deletion_in_index:found] of 256 | 697 [run faf02d89/blame_mutant_runtime_miss_deletion_in_index:reported] | 41,284 [run faf02d89/blame_mutant_runtime_miss_deletion_in_index:lines_served] |
| A restored element blamed to its restorer, not its root | 207 [run faf02d89/blame_mutant_diff_restored_as_restorer:found] of 256 | 414 [run faf02d89/blame_mutant_runtime_restored_as_restorer:reported] | 41,024 [run faf02d89/blame_mutant_runtime_restored_as_restorer:lines_served] |

- A history where a fault was never found is one where it never applied: no deletion of a
  restored element, or no restoration, in its 40 steps.
- **Never served:** under the runtime check, every blame equals the rebuild's (a wrong one
  fails the history).
- `blame_runtime_check_samples` shows the sampling. At 1 in 3, a restored-as-restorer map is
  read unchecked on the second blame. The third blame catches it: it is reported, and the
  rebuild is served.
- The run before the fix (`a0c863df`, at `d8b2d3a`) caught the same faults at about the same
  rates.

## The soak, with this change alone

`crates/base/tests/soak.rs`, `soak_32`, `SOAK_SECS=600`, `SOAK_SEED=1`, a build node, `--cpus 4
--mem 8G`, release. The two jobs **ran at the same time** on the same node: v0.9.4 (job
`15d633b9`) and v0.9.4 plus this change (`3a3f9cd0`, at `d8b2d3a`).

| | v0.9.4 | v0.9.4 + this change |
|---|---|---|
| Calls in 600 s | 117,096 [run 15d633b9/soak_32:calls] | 117,762 [run 3a3f9cd0/soak_32:calls] |
| Calls/s, first window | 850 [run 15d633b9/soak_32:first_calls_per_s] | 858 [run 3a3f9cd0/soak_32:first_calls_per_s] |
| Calls/s, last 150 s | 77 [run 15d633b9/soak_32:tail_calls_per_s] | 78 [run 3a3f9cd0/soak_32:tail_calls_per_s] |
| Slowdown (%; check: at most 200) | 1,108 [run 15d633b9/soak_32:slowdown_percent] | 1,105 [run 3a3f9cd0/soak_32:slowdown_percent] |

- **Blame's share of the slowdown is nil:** the two runs are the same within noise. The soak
  blames every line every 250 calls and never after an outside edit, so its map was already
  kept. A blame of every line costs about 1.1 ms at these sizes (above): about 4 µs per call,
  spread over 250 calls [derived].
- The soak's `blame` phase timer (0.12 ms per call in the first window; 1.8 and 2.4 ms in the
  last; printed lines, not run records) is mostly the **flush** before each blame: a
  write-back, O(the engine state), which the incremental write-back addresses.
